source.title: Fingerprint, Not Blueprint: How Positional Schemes Set the Default Spectral Algebra of Attention

page_placements.theme: Developmental signatures of induction-circuit formation (LLC, susceptibilities, influence functions, spectra)

record.file_problem: None; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures induction-related circuits and their training dynamics, but refines the account: the spectral profile follows or accompanies circuit formation, and constrained training reroutes around spectral channels while paying a formation-time cost.
record.gate_note: The paper reports checkpoint measurements of previous-token and induction behavior, an in-context-learning proxy, K-composition wiring, and interventions that change induction loss or formation time. It does not report a training-loss bump. Its cited results from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses QK spectral measures and ablations to check previous-token to induction K-composition in GPT-2, Pythia and Llama. It tracks previous-token, induction and ICL-proxy formation over Pythia checkpoints. It also trains two-layer attention-only models under different positional schemes and constraints. It is a different method aimed at the same circuit and formation questions; it does not argue against any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors' central claim is that the positional scheme sets the default spectral algebra of attention heads. The rotational signature is born at the random-matrix null and locks in with circuit formation, not before it, and is then sculpted after function. In toy models no spectral channel is necessary: training reroutes around each ban at a significant formation-time cost.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses QK spectral measurements, checkpoint tracking, targeted operator ablations, and constrained-from-scratch training; it is not a direct replication of the original phase-change measurement. It does not report the original training-loss bump or the later-versus-earlier token loss comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: Formation timing changes with positional scheme and spectral constraint. The checkpoint analysis reports that the spectral signature and behavior are simultaneous at the available half-doubling resolution; it cannot order them within the formation window.

fits_no_version.finding: The previous-token head's rope_imag_frac percentile goes from 0.03–0.04 to 0.90–0.99 during formation, simultaneously with behaviour. It does not predict the eventual prev head beforehand.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight-spectral signatures of induction-circuit heads emerge with, not before, circuit behaviour and do not predict which head will form.

fits_no_version.finding: Population-median Dhead is suppressed below the Ginibre null (0.61 → 0.395/0.453) only after formation, while prev heads retain rotational structure.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-formation sculpting of QK spectra differentiates circuit heads from the bulk.

record.problems: The checkpoint analysis has 22 checkpoints per model and cannot resolve ordering within the formation window. It reports no training-loss bump. The constrained-training results use a toy random-map task with n=5 seeds per cell. The authors note that single-head ablations miss circuit composition and that the tested positional/model-family coverage is limited.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported result was omitted.

untested.parts: K-composition and token-level [A][B]…[A]→[B] behaviour are not checked in the attention-only toy models; only the presence of strong prev and induction heads is reported.
No training-loss bump is reported, and there is no numeric ICL-proxy trajectory.
Entire version: no measure of the share of in-context learning carried by induction heads.
Non-transformer architectures, other modalities, and multiple training runs of the same pretrained model.
Training-data properties are not varied; only positional scheme and spectral penalties are.
Ordering within the formation window below half-doubling checkpoint resolution.

missing.what: Across all heads, 92–99% move <0.01 in induction loss under Im(Mt) ablation. Other prev>0.5 heads show ≈0 effects, suggesting redundancy in a multi-head circuit.
No numeric values for induction/prefix-matching score, ICL proxy (second- minus first-copy NLL) or K-composition across checkpoints; only qualitative timing in Fig. 4 text.

record.verdict_notes: Induction heads are a tool and an object here, not the main topic. Pretrained-model rows are relinked from V1 to V4 because V1 names attention-only transformers; only the toy models fit V1. Tranche changed from T5 to T2 because nothing argues a version is wrong. Rows r9/r10 test antisymmetry necessity, not induction presence.

versions.untested_parts: The study checks K-composition wiring and causal effects on induction tasks, but does not directly establish every part of the [A][B] … [A] → [B] token-level mechanism in its constrained toy models.
The study tracks previous-token and induction behavior and an ICL proxy, but does not report a training-loss bump or the later-token-versus-earlier-token loss comparison specified in the claim.
It does not measure what fraction of large-transformer in-context learning is carried by induction heads or report token-index loss as a measure of most ICL.

The induction-related causal tests cover GPT-2, Pythia-410m, Pythia-1.4B, and Llama-3-8B; the paper does not test other architectures or modalities, or establish universality across all model families and runs.
Training-data properties are not varied systematically; the constrained-training tests vary positional scheme and spectral constraints on a per-sequence random-map task.
The study does not compare few-shot task learning through induction heads with learning through other heads or mechanisms.
The checkpoint spacing is described as half-doubling resolution; the study cannot resolve the ordering of behavior and spectral signature within the same formation window.
